title: Naturality of the map from first Cech cohomology to H^1
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let U = {U_i} be an open covering of X. For every O_X-module H there is a canonical homomorphism c_H from the first Cech cohomology group of U with values in H to H^1(X,H) [pqf-def-cohomology], and these homomorphisms are natural in H: for every morphism of O_X-modules phi: H -> H', the map from the first Cech cohomology group of U with values in H to that with values in H' induced by the cochain map (a_{i_0 i_1}) -> (phi(a_{i_0 i_1})), followed by c_{H'}, equals c_H followed by H^1(X,phi).

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EQ (cohomology-lemma-cech-cohomology): the transformation of functors from the Cech complex to RGamma, giving canonical maps natural in the module

proof.text: Fix an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal H$. Since $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ has enough injectives, choose an injective resolution $\mathcal H\to\mathcal I^\bullet$. Form the first-quadrant double complex $D_{\mathcal H}^{p,q}=\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I^q)$, with the Cech differential horizontally and the resolution differential vertically, and its total complex $T_{\mathcal H}$. Restriction of global sections gives a cochain map $\alpha_{\mathcal H}:\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)\to T_{\mathcal H}$ in Cech degree zero; the resolution map gives a cochain map $\beta_{\mathcal H}:\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal H)\to T_{\mathcal H}$ in resolution degree zero. In each case the other differential of the image is zero, respectively by the sheaf gluing condition and because $\mathcal H\to\mathcal I^0\to\mathcal I^1$ is a complex.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EQ (lemma-cech-cohomology), proof, construction of the double complex and maps alpha and beta

proof.text: For each $q$, the $q$-th horizontal row has $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I^q)=0$ for $p>0$ because $\mathcal I^q$ is injective, while its degree-zero cohomology is $\mathcal I^q(X)$: a Cech zero-cocycle is precisely a family of local sections agreeing on every overlap, and the sheaf axiom glues it uniquely. Apply the row-first spectral sequence of this first-quadrant double complex. Its first page is concentrated in horizontal degree zero and there is no differential entering or leaving that column on later pages; its edge map is induced by $\alpha_{\mathcal H}$. The spectral sequence converges to $H^*(T_{\mathcal H})$, so $H^n(\alpha_{\mathcal H})$ is an isomorphism for every $n$.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EQ proof, Lemma 01EP (lemma-injective-trivial-cech) and the row-acyclic total-complex argument

proof.text: Define $c_{\mathcal H}$ on first cohomology as $H^1(\alpha_{\mathcal H})^{-1}\circ H^1(\beta_{\mathcal H})$, followed by the canonical identification $H^1(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))=H^1(X,\mathcal H)$. The inverse exists by step 2. Both maps entering the formula are canonical in the derived category: changing the injective resolution gives the same morphism through a comparison map of resolutions, and the comparison maps induce the standard identifications for the right-derived global-sections functor.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EQ proof, final paragraph: beta followed by inverse alpha in the derived category

proof.text: Given $\varphi:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H'$, choose injective resolutions and lift $\varphi$ to a cochain map $\widetilde\varphi:\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$. Termwise restriction and the Cech cochain functor produce $T(\widetilde\varphi):T_{\mathcal H}\to T_{\mathcal H'}$. The square with the two $\alpha$ maps commutes in every degree because restriction commutes with $\widetilde\varphi^q$; the square with the two $\beta$ maps commutes because $\widetilde\varphi^0$ lifts $\varphi$. Thus on $H^1$, using the formula of step 3 and the injective-resolution formula for $H^1(X,\varphi)$, one obtains $c_{\mathcal H'}\circ\check H^1(\mathcal U,\varphi)=H^1(X,\varphi)\circ c_{\mathcal H}$. This also supplies the functoriality verification omitted in the source proof.
